 Gabe Hauari USA TODAY Oct. 21, 2026 Updated Oct. 22, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET Hear this story More than 4 million tubes of toothpaste have been recalled nationwide, including some popular children's brands.
 Pritam International Private Limited initiated the voluntary recall on Sept. 10, according to an enforcement report from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The FDA classified the recall as Class II on Oct. 19.
 The FDA's website lists a Class II recall as "a situation in which use of or exposure to a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or where the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote."
 According to the FDA, the recall includes multiple varieties of Brush Buddies kids toothpaste distributed nationwide, including some character-themed and ice-cream flavors. The recall also included two types of Evo products marketed for teeth whitening and sensitivity, and two Aru products marketed for gum health and cavity protection.
 The FDA told USA TODAY via email on Thursday, Oct. 22, the reason for the recall is "deviations from current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements." According to the agency's website, the CGMP regulations for drugs contains "minimum requirements for the methods, facilities, and controls used in manufacturing, processing and packaging of a drug product." It also help ensure a product is safe for use and that it has the ingredients and strength it claims to have.
